methods.name: Stage-Progression

methods.name: Peer-Median

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Hystar, a Series B climate and energy company founded by Alejandro Oyarce Barnett, has raised $36M to date. Valuation analysis draws from a peer set of 9 comparable companies—1 public (LNZA) and 8 private—including stage-adjacent players such as KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, Amogy, Helion, and Redwood Materials.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $36M total raised as a proxy base value and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B to subsequent-stage advancement, yielding $68M. Peer-median methodology anchors to a median valuation of $1.0B across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables (KoBold at $3.0B, Electric Hydrogen at $1.0B, Amogy at $700M), establishing a $700M–$3.0B range.

The triangulated analysis produces a low of $58M, median of $534M, and high of $1.1B. The wide spread reflects material uncertainty inherent in early-stage climate tech, where peer valuations span nearly 4x and revenue visibility remains limited. Stage-progression yields a tighter, more conservative estimate; peer medians reflect significant capital availability in the sector but also wide dispersion in company maturity and technical risk. Key sensitivities include technology validation timelines, capital intensity of scaling, and policy-dependent demand for hydrogen solutions. The $534M median represents the center of the implied range but should be weighted against specific commercial and technical risks not captured in comparable multiples alone.
